Admittedly, certain land owned by the petitioner was acquired vide notifications dated 15.12.2006 and 14.12.2007 issued under Sections 4 and 6 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 for the public purpose namely, for development of Sector 26, Rohtak (the residential and institutional Sector)
respectively, followed by award dated 03.07.2009 03.07.2009,, whereby, the Land Acquisition Collector awarded compensation @ of Rs.
Rs.20,00,000/--
per acre.
Feeling dissatisfied, the petitioner/landowners filed petition u under nder Section 18 of the 1894 Act, which was decided by the Reference Court vide award dated 05.07.2014.

3. Aggrieved thereof, thereof, the land owners filed Regular First Appeal No.1537/2016 which was allowed vide order dated 16.03.2022, enhancing the compensation from Rs.20 lakhs per acre to Rs.42.51 lakhs per acre.

Thereafter, the petitioner filed execution application bearing No. EXE/654/2022 before the learned Addl. District Judge, Rohtak in February 2024 seeking execution of the judgment and decree,
however, the said execution proceedings are being repeatedly adjourned and are now pending for 09.04.2025, thereby, delaying the disbursal of enhanced amount of compensation to the petitioner/landowners.

5. I have heard the learned counsel for the petitioner.

6. A perusal of record shows that execution petition (Annexure P-3) filed by the petitioner on 14.11.2024, is still pending and the petitioner is waiting to get their full amount of compensation on the basis of decision dated 16.03.2022 passed by this Court.
7.

In Rahul S. Shah Vs. Jinendra Kumar Gandhi and others (2021) 6 SCC 418, the Hon'ble Supreme Court held as follow:-
"That the executing Court must dispose of execution proceeding within 6 months from the date of filing which may be extended only by recording reasons in writing for such delay."
